body:
## Current checkpoint: actual-orbit power estimates and direct closing attacks

**Full Collatz remains OPEN.** This checkpoint adds a written power-law discrepancy theorem for every supplied distinct ordinary odd-orbit segment, its exact-edge Lean core, and three parallel attempts to complete the same-source entropy, sibling, and whole-word merger routes. No universal descent, escape exclusion, or complete nontrivial-cycle exclusion was obtained.

## 1. Polynomial phase discrepancy on every actual distinct segment

Let q_0,...,q_N be positive integers with exact edges 2^(g_i) q_(i+1)=3q_i+1 and distinct first N states. Their leading phases theta_i={log_2 q_i} obey an irrational rotation with corrections whose total is at most H_N/(3 log 2).

A continued-fraction block argument, combined with Rhin's exponent 7.616, proves

~~~text
D_N <= C_R ((1+log N)/N)^(1/8.616) = O(N^(-1/9)).
~~~

This is uniform over the original source and the starting position of the window. It uses no random-parity premise and no averaging over starting integers. A separate elementary version has fully explicit O(1/log N) constants. The power estimate leaves the absolute literature constant numerically unspecified.

The precise Rhin input was read in Lagarias–Soundararajan, Lemma 5.3, equation (5.11), which reproduces Rhin's inequality (8). Their distinct stochastic-seed theorem is not used. Rhin's original book chapter was not independently reconstructed.

For binary one-run count R, the same argument proves

~~~text
(1/N) #{i<N : R(q_i)<=S}
  = O_S(N^(-1/9) (log N)^(2S-1)).

For 0<c<1/4 and S_N=floor(c floor(log_2(N)/9)):
(1/N) #{i<N : R(q_i)<=S_N}
  = O_c(N^(-(1-H_2(2c))/9)).

For rho>1 and 0<kappa<log_2(rho)/36:
(1/N) sum_(i<N) rho^R(q_i) >= C_(rho,kappa) N^kappa
for sufficiently large N.
~~~

This improves the asymptotic occupation rate beyond fresh PR176's explicit fixed-S O(N/log N) count. PR176's logarithmic-horizon sparse-return descent and PR177's fixed-separation finite-core theorem retain geometric information not supplied by phase distribution.

The qualified actual terminal-energy lower bound inherits a polynomial rate. The required opposing upper bound remains unproved: PR175's exact commutator and PR177's new finite-Green depth/time profile retain the escape coefficient, including in the omitted full-potential tail.

[Complete phase, run and energy proof](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/7e4569476e152f6b8537bdc1711df595ec1ffd89/research/whole-repo-synthesis-20261122/phase/EFFECTIVE_PHASE_AND_RUNS.md)

## 2. Exact natural-number edges to the Fourier bound, in Lean

The composed public theorem proves, for each integer frequency h,

~~~text
|exp(2 pi i h log_2 3)-1|
  * |sum_(i<N) exp(2 pi i h log_2 q_i)|
<= 2 + (2 pi |h| / (3 log 2)) H_N.
~~~

A second theorem replaces H_N by 1+log N. The proof derives the phase recurrence internally from literal ordinary edges. Reciprocal rearrangement, the logarithmic edge identity, the whole correction budget, integer-frequency periodicity and the finite complex telescope are included.

**Both new modules compiled; all 12 public declarations were audited.** These are ten theorems and two definitions. The only axiom dependencies are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No admitted proof or new theorem axiom is introduced.

Continued fractions, Rhin, discrepancy, prefix counting, and the infinite canonical applications remain written mathematics.

## 3. All inverse horizons, with the same actual endpoints

Under the pinned ordinary canonical inputs, let a_i be the canonical probability of the actual predecessor and D_k the product through k. The exact telescope gives D_k decreasing to D_infinity>0.

For the marked actual reversed window from q_(j+m) to q_j and the matching canonical inverse chain, averaged over j<L,

~~~text
KL(P_(L,m) || Q_(L,m))
 <= b_L = (1/L) sum_(j<L) log(D_j/D_infinity) -> 0,

TV(P_(L,m),Q_(L,m)) <= b_L,
uniformly over every m.
~~~

The endpoint is the same actual time ensemble. This transfers bounded observables and normalized finite-resolution entropy. The normalized real fibres also converge along the actual orbit to a common law.

A finite positive compact canonical density E would give the exact stationary identity H(e|x)=a log 2-log 3. Two positive branches force a>log_2 3, contradicting the actual mean-gap ceiling. **Passing the actual time limit to that same kernel remains unproved.** Moving traces retain the original clock in their precision, and ordinary full support can degenerate along the escaping sequence.

[Inverse-window transfer, entropy criterion and fibre limit](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/7e4569476e152f6b8537bdc1711df595ec1ffd89/research/whole-repo-synthesis-20261122/entropy/CANONICAL_TIME_ENTROPY_ATTEMPT.md)

## 4. Whole high-spike sectors and complete alternative source words

The sibling lane combines credited prior PR185 finite-spine concentration with PR175's moving-trace theorem to obtain uniformity over an entire fixed-height spike sector. The anchor clock remains. Fresh PR175's payoff-weighted witness-depth restriction is compared explicitly; it does not furnish the required sibling lower bound.

The arithmetic lane allows the entire source word and both merger clocks to vary. It derives the exact smaller-ancestor correction reservoir, retains every actual parity, and identifies the unproved existence statement. A complete finite control proves that all smaller sources at every inverse clock avoid target 1263's clocks 0–24; the first merger is at 25 and descent at 26. This target converges.

The new sparse-return theorem also restricts a sufficiently large least bad target to at most |H_S|+1 low-run visits in its first floor(C log t)+1 odd states. The exceptional set contains {1,...,2S}; using the forward run-growth estimate to choose a larger cutoff therefore makes the tested separation exceptional. The phase and sparse-return scarcity bounds do not contradict each other.
